(i) This question paper contains 35 questions. All questions are compulsory.
(ii) This question paper is divided into FIVE Sections – Section A, B, C, D and E.
(iii) In Section A - Q. No. 1 to 18 are Multiple Choice (MCQ) type questions carrying 1 mark each.
(iv) In Section B - Q. No. 19 to 25 are Very Short Answer (VSA) type questions carrying 2 marks each.
(v) In Section C - Q. No. 26 to 30 are Very Short Answer (SA) type questions carrying 3 marks each.
(vi) In Section D - Q. No. 31 to 32 are case-based type questions carrying 4 marks each.
(vii) In Section E - Q. No. 33 to 35 are Long Answer (LA) type questions carrying 5 marks each.
(viii) There is no overall choice. However, an internal choice has been provided in 2 question in Section B, 2 questions in Section C, 2 questions in Section D and 2 questions in Section E.
(ix) Use of log tables and calculators is NOT allowed.

questions.stem: Write two difference between DNA and RNA.
questions.solution:
The structural differences between DNA and RNA are as follows :
DNA | RNA
1. The sugar moiety in DNA molecules is $\beta$-D-2 deoxyribose. | The sugar moiety in RNA molecules is $\beta$-D ribose.
2. DNA contains thyamine (T). It does not contain Uracil (U). | RNA contains uracil (U). It does not contain thymine (T).
3. The helical structure of DNA is double-stranded. | The helical structure of RNA is single-stranded.

When 19.5 g of $\mathrm{F-CH_2-COOH}$ (Molar mass = 78 g $\mathrm{mol^{-1}}$), is dissolved in 500 g of water, the depression in freezing point at observed to be $1^\circ$C. Calculate the degree of dissociation of $\mathrm{F-CH_2-COOH}$.
[Given : $K_f$ for water = 1.86 K kg $\mathrm{mol^{-1}}$]
questions.solution:
It is given that :
$w_1 = 500$ g, $w_2 = 19.5$ g
$K_f = 1.86\ \mathrm{K\,kg\,mol^{-1}}$, $\Delta T_f = 1$ K
We know that : $M_2 = \frac{K_f \times w_2 \times 1000}{\Delta T_f \times w_1}$ ½
$= \frac{1.86\ \mathrm{K\,kg\,mol^{-1}} \times 19.5\ \mathrm{g} \times 1000\ \mathrm{g\,kg^{-1}}}{500\ \mathrm{g} \times 1\ \mathrm{K}} = 72.54\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$ ½
Therefore, observed molar mass of $\mathrm{CH_2FCOOH}$, $(M_2)_{obs} = 72.54\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$
The calculated molar mass of $\mathrm{CH_2FCOOH}$ is :
$(M_2)_{cal} = 14 + 19 + 12 + 16 + 16 + 1 = 78\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$
Therefore, van't Hoff factor, $i = \frac{(M_2)_{cal}}{(M_2)_{obs}} = \frac{78\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}}{72.54\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}} = 1.0753$ ½
Let $\alpha$ be the degree of dissociation of $\mathrm{CH_2FCOOH}$
$\mathrm{CH_2FCOOH \rightleftharpoons CH_2FCOO^- + H^+}$
Initial conc. : $C$ mol $\mathrm{L^{-1}}$, 0, 0
At equilibrium : $C(1-\alpha)$, $C\alpha$, $C\alpha$; Total $= C(1+\alpha)$
$\therefore\ i = \frac{C(1+\alpha)}{C}$ ½
$\Rightarrow i = 1 + \alpha$ ½
$\Rightarrow \alpha = i - 1 = 1.0753 - 1 = 0.0753$
$\Rightarrow \alpha = 7.53\%$ ½

questions.stem:
The carbon - oxygen double bond is polarised in aldehydes and ketones due to higher electronegativity of oxygen relative to carbon. Therefore they undergo nucleophilic addition reactions with a number of nucleophiles such HCN, $\mathrm{NaHSO_3}$, alcohols, ammonia derivatives and Grignard reagents. Aldehydes are easily oxidised by mid oxidising agents as compared to ketones. The carbonyl group of carboxylic acid does not give reactions of aldehydes and ketones. Carboxylic acids are considerable more acidic than alcohols and most of simple phenols.

Answer the following :
(a) Write the name of the product when an aldehyde reacts with excess alcohol in presence of dry HCl.
(b) Why carboxylic acid is a stronger acid than phenol ?
(c) (i) Arrange the following compounds in increasing order of their reactivity towards $\mathrm{CH_3MgBr}$ :
$\mathrm{CH_3CHO}$, $\mathrm{(CH_3)_3C-CO-CH_3}$, $\mathrm{CH_3-CO-CH_3}$
(ii) Write a chemical test of distinguish between propanal and propanone.
OR
(c) Write the main product in the following :
(i) [structure shown in figure] reacting with $\mathrm{[Ag(NH_3)_2]^+}$
(ii) [structure shown in figure] reacting with $\mathrm{H_2NCONHNH_2}$
questions.solution:
(a) Acetal (see figure).
(b) Because carboxylate ion is much more resonance stabilised than phenoxide ion, as the negative charge is delocalised over two electronegative O-atoms in the carboxylate anion, while in phenol the negative charge is delocalised over only one O-atom and electropositive carbon atom.
(c) (i) $\mathrm{(CH_3)_3C-CO-CH_3 < CH_3-CO-CH_3 < CH_3CHO}$
(ii) Propanal, being an aldehyde, reduces Fehling's solution to a red-brown ppt of $\mathrm{Cu_2O}$, but propanone, being a ketone, does not.
Propanal, being an aldehyde, reduces Tollens' reagent to a silver mirror but propanone, being a ketone, does not.
Propanone responds to the Iodoform test whereas propanal does not.
OR
(c) (i), (ii) : see figure.

questions.stem:
Carbohydrates are optically active polyhydroxy aldehydes and ketones. They are also called saccharides. All those carbohydrates which reduce Fehling's solution and Tollen's reagent are referred to as reducing sugars. Glucose, the most important source of energy for mammals, is obtained by the hydrolysis of starch. Vitamins are accessory food factors required in the diet. Proteins are the polymers of $\alpha$-amino acids and perform various structural and dynamic functions in the organisms. Deficiency of vitamins leads to many diseases.

(a) The penta-acetate of glucose does not react with hydroxylamine. What does it indicate?
(b) Why cannot vitamin C be stored in our body?
(c) Define the following as related to proteins :
(i) Peptide linkage
(ii) Denaturation
OR
(c) Define the following as related to carbohydrates:
(i) Anomers
(ii) Glycosidic linkage
questions.solution:
(a) It indicates the absence of a free $\mathrm{-CHO}$ group.
(b) Because it is a water soluble vitamin and is readily excreted in urine.
(c) (i) Peptide linkage : The amide formed between the $\mathrm{-COOH}$ group of one molecule of an amino acid and the $\mathrm{-NH_2}$ group of another molecule of the amino acid by the elimination of a water molecule is called a peptide linkage. (see figure)
(ii) Denaturation : When a protein in its native form is subjected to a physical change, like change in temperature, or a chemical change, like change in pH, the hydrogen bonds are disturbed. Due to this, globules unfold and the helix gets uncoiled and the protein loses its biological activity. This is called denaturation of protein.
OR
(c) (i) $\alpha$-glucose and $\beta$-D-glucose, which have configuration isomerism at the $\mathrm{C_1}$ carbon, are known as anomers.
(ii) A linkage between two monosaccharide units through an oxygen atom is called a glycosidic linkage.

questions.stem:
(a) (I) Account for the following :
(i) $E^{\circ}$ value for $\mathrm{Mn^{3+}/Mn^{2+}}$ couple is much more positive than that for $\mathrm{Cr^{3+}/Cr^{2+}}$.
(ii) $\mathrm{Sc^{3+}}$ is colourless whereas $\mathrm{Ti^{3+}}$ is coloured in an aqueous solution.
(iii) Actinoids show wide range of oxidation states.
(II) Write the chemical equations for the preparation of $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ from $\mathrm{MnO_2}$.
questions.solution:
(I) (i) Much larger third ionisation energy of Mn (where the required change is $d^{5}$ to $d^{4}$) is mainly responsible for this. This also explains why the $+3$ state of Mn is of little importance.
(ii) $\mathrm{Sc^{3+}}$ is colourless due to the absence of unpaired electrons as it attains $3d^{0}$ configuration, while $\mathrm{Ti^{3+}}$ has $3d^{1}$ configuration.
(iii) Due to comparable energies of $5f$, $6d$ and $7s$ orbitals.
(II) $\mathrm{2MnO_2 + 4KOH + O_2 \longrightarrow 2K_2MnO_4 + 2H_2O}$
$\mathrm{3MnO_4^{2-} + 4H^+ \longrightarrow 2MnO_4^- + MnO_2 + 2H_2O}$

questions.stem:
(a) (I) Give reasons:
(i) Aniline on nitration gives good amount of m-nitroaniline, though $\mathrm{-NH_2}$ group is o/p directing in electrophilic substitution reactions.
(ii) $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2NH}$ is more basic than $\mathrm{(CH_3)_3N}$ in an aqueous solution.
(iii) Ammonolysis of alkyl halides is not a good method to prepare pure primary amines.
(II) Write the reaction involved in the following :
(i) Carbyl amine test
(ii) Gabriel phthalimide synthesis
questions.solution:
(I) (i) See figure. In strongly acidic medium aniline is protonated to form the anilinium ion, in which the $\mathrm{-\overset{+}{N}H_3}$ group acts as meta directing.
$\mathrm{C_6H_5NH_2 + H^+HSO_4^- \longrightarrow C_6H_5\overset{+}{N}H_3\,HSO_4^-}$
(ii) It is the combination of the electron releasing nature of the alkyl group, H-bonding and steric factors that determines the stability of the ammonium cations formed in solution; therefore $\mathrm{Et_2NH > Et_3N > EtNH_2}$ is the order of $K_b$.
(iii) Alkyl halide on reaction with $\mathrm{NH_3}$ undergoes nucleophilic substitution reaction and forms $1^\circ$, $2^\circ$, $3^\circ$ amines and finally the quaternary ammonium salt, which is difficult to separate.
(II) (i) $\mathrm{R-NH_2 + CHCl_3 + 3KOH \xrightarrow{Heat} R-NC + 3KCl + 3H_2O}$
(ii) See figure.
questions.or_stem:
(b) (I) Write the structures of A, B and C in the following reactions :
(i) [reaction scheme shown in figure]
(ii) [reaction scheme shown in figure]
(II) Why aniline does not undergo Friedal-Crafts reaction ?
(III) Arrange the following in increasing order of their boiling point:
$\mathrm{C_2H_5OH}$, $\mathrm{C_2H_5NH_2}$, $\mathrm{(C_2H_5)_3N}$
questions.or_solution:
(I) (i), (ii) : see figure.
(II) Aniline, being a Lewis base, reacts with the Lewis acid $\mathrm{AlCl_3}$ to form a salt.
$\mathrm{C_6H_5NH_2 + AlCl_3 \longrightarrow C_6H_5\overset{+}{N}H_2\,\overset{-}{A}lCl_3}$
As a result, N of aniline acquires a positive charge and hence it acts as a strong deactivating group for electrophilic substitution reaction; consequently, aniline does not undergo Friedel-Crafts reaction.
(III) $\mathrm{(C_2H_3)_3N < C_2H_5NH_2 < C_2H_5OH}$
